hyps.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 receives no input, so a conv on edge 4 contributes nothing.
If node 1 is disconnected from the input, edge 2 only propagates zeros and the edit is ineffective.
Replacing a missing edge with a conv adds a new informative path, a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
Deleting the strongest operation on an output edge costs more than deleting a weak or parameter-free one.
With edge 5 already absent, removing the direct edge leaves only edge 4 to reach the output, sharply degrading the cell.
If edge 1 is also none, removing edge 0 kills nodes 1 and 2 entirely, leaving only the direct path.
When the node-2 output path is missing, the direct edge carries more of the computation, so adding a conv there helps more.
Reconnecting node 1 with a conv reactivates edges 2 and 4, yielding a larger gain than swapping an existing op.
Diminishing returns: when the direct path already has a 3x3 conv, another conv into the output adds less.
Restoring the node 0 to node 2 connection with a conv adds a new path and helps more than replacing an existing op.
